alternative: Pass the varying step into a stable public method as a callback or delegate object (Strategy / Execute Around), or keep the varying behaviour in a separate collaborator; if a base class must be subclassed, use a documented `_impl`-suffixed hook and accept that the non-virtual contract is convention only (nothing prevents a subclass, monkey-patching or Object.defineProperty from replacing the entry point).
idiom_name: convention-only hook methods (`_impl`) - the non-virtual guarantee cannot be expressed
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no virtual, final, protected or abstract: every method lives on the prototype and can be replaced by any subclass or by monkey-patching at runtime. Private `#` methods are genuinely private, but private names are neither inherited nor overridable, so a base wrapper calling this.#hook() would always run the base's own implementation - the strongest visibility in the language cannot be an extension point (MDN private elements). The workable approximation is a stable public entry point that calls an `_impl`-suffixed, documented hook, with the invariant in the wrapper; prefer composition or callbacks, and reserve the base-class shape for framework-driven extension points where the framework (not the class) calls the hooks.
pitfalls: Subclasses can override the entry point itself - the pattern's guarantee is a naming convention and no tool checks it in plain JavaScript.
Private `#` methods cannot serve as hooks: they are not inherited and not overridable, so the base's own hook always runs.
Patching the prototype after construction silently changes the wrapper for every existing instance.
